text: Most code generation starts with a prompt. Our workflow starts with real enterprise governance context.
A Coding Agent queries DataHub through MCP, then generates TeaQL applications inside a controlled network.
This is the real payment_transactions dataset running in our DataHub instance.
Its schema exposes four business fields and marks payment_account as PII.
The Agent maps each field into TeaQL and turns governance policy into _audit_mask_fields.
DataHub lineage reports zero upstream entities, so the model does not invent a payment-to-user relationship.
The generator runs on 127.0.0.1. The model never leaves the controlled network.
Java and Rust are generated from empty directories, then a second run verifies deterministic output.
Raw audit events stay on a controlled forensic path. Analytics systems receive only SafeAuditEvent.
SafeAuditEvent reads the generated audit_mask_fields policy and masks payment_account before output.
Real Java and Rust tests prove masking is enabled and the raw account never reaches safe output.
We also test the failure path. When DataHub returns entity not found, the Agent refuses to generate.
Both business-field and relationship arrays remain empty, and the mechanical assertion passes.
Enterprise DataHub governance now constrains the model, generated code, and runtime behavior.
